=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tx "x = "
text ty "y = "
text tz "z = "
text s0 "lions, tigers, and"
text s1 "bears, oh my!"
text s2 "(from the \"Wizard of OZ\")"
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note sort3 orders three longs with three compare-exchanges and prints them as x, y, z
fn sort3 x long y long z long to void
if gt x y
t = x
x = y
y = t
end
if gt y z
t = y
y = z
z = t
end
if gt x y
t = x
x = y
y = t
end
emit tx
emiti x
emit nl
emit ty
emiti y
emit nl
emit tz
emiti z
emit nl
end
note str writes text number k (0, 1 or 2); a text cannot be chosen by index, so this is an if chain
fn str k ulong to void
if eq k 0
emit s0
end
if eq k 1
emit s1
end
if eq k 2
emit s2
end
end
note cmpb compares two byte strings: negative, zero or positive, like C's strcmp on unsigned bytes
fn cmpb a view uchar * b view uchar * to long
for i ulong len a
if ge i len b
ret 1
end
if ne get a i get b i
ret sub long get a i long get b i
end
end
if lt len a len b
ret -1
end
ret 0
end
note gtk says whether text j sorts after text k; the three pairs are spelled out for the same reason
fn gtk j ulong k ulong to bool
c = long 0
if and eq j 0 eq k 1
c = cmpb s0 s1
end
if and eq j 1 eq k 0
c = cmpb s1 s0
end
if and eq j 0 eq k 2
c = cmpb s0 s2
end
if and eq j 2 eq k 0
c = cmpb s2 s0
end
if and eq j 1 eq k 2
c = cmpb s1 s2
end
if and eq j 2 eq k 1
c = cmpb s2 s1
end
ret gt c 0
end
fn showk x ulong y ulong z ulong to void
emit tx
str x
emit nl
emit ty
str y
emit nl
emit tz
str z
emit nl
end
note sorts the strings the same way, by swapping which text each variable names
fn sorts to void
x = ulong 0
y = ulong 1
z = ulong 2
showk x y z
if gtk x y
t = x
x = y
y = t
end
if gtk y z
t = y
y = z
z = t
end
if gtk x y
t = x
x = y
y = t
end
showk x y z
end
fn main to int
emit tx
emiti 77444
emit nl
emit ty
emiti -12
emit nl
emit tz
emiti 0
emit nl
sort3 77444 -12 0
sorts
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
x = 77444
y = -12
z = 0
x = -12
y = 0
z = 77444
x = lions, tigers, and
y = bears, oh my!
z = (from the "Wizard of OZ")
x = (from the "Wizard of OZ")
y = bears, oh my!
z = lions, tigers, and
</pre>
